q.en: How many surahs are there in the Quran?

e.en: The Mushaf contains 114 surahs, from Al-Fatihah to An-Nas.

q.en: Which surah opens the Quran?

e.en: Al-Fatihah, 'The Opening', is the first surah and is recited in every rak'ah of salah.

q.en: Which is the longest surah of the Quran?

e.en: Al-Baqarah has 286 verses, the most of any surah.

q.en: Which is the shortest surah of the Quran?

e.en: Al-Kawthar has only three short verses.

q.en: Which surah does not begin with Bismillah?

e.en: At-Tawbah (Bara'ah) is the only surah that does not open with Bismillah.

q.en: In which surah does Bismillah appear twice?

e.en: Besides its opening, Bismillah appears inside Sulayman's letter to the Queen of Sheba.

q.en: What were the first words revealed to the Prophet ﷺ?

en: "Iqra" — Read in the name of your Lord

e.en: The first revelation was the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq in the cave of Hira.

q.en: On which night did the Quran begin to be revealed?

e.en: Allah says: 'Indeed, We sent it down on the Night of Decree.'

q.en: In which month was the Quran first revealed?

e.en: 'The month of Ramadan in which the Quran was revealed…'

q.en: In which surah is Ayat al-Kursi?

e.en: Ayat al-Kursi is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah.

q.en: Which surah did the Prophet ﷺ say is equal to one third of the Quran?

e.en: The Prophet ﷺ said Surah Al-Ikhlas equals a third of the Quran.

q.en: Memorising the first ten verses of which surah protects from the Dajjal?

e.en: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever memorises the first ten verses of Al-Kahf is protected from the Dajjal.

q.en: How many juz (parts) is the Quran divided into?

e.en: The Quran is divided into 30 equal parts (juz / para) for recitation.

q.en: Which angel brought the revelation to the Prophet ﷺ?

e.en: Jibril (Gabriel) brought the Quran down to the heart of the Prophet ﷺ.

q.en: Who is the only woman mentioned by name in the Quran?

e.en: Maryam, mother of Isa (peace be upon them), is named in the Quran and a surah carries her name.

q.en: Which prophet is mentioned by name most often in the Quran?

e.en: Musa (peace be upon him) is named more than any other prophet, over 130 times.

q.en: Which surah is named after the ant?

e.en: An-Naml (27) tells how an ant warned the others of Sulayman's army.

q.en: In which surah is 'Which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?' repeated?

e.en: The verse is repeated 31 times in Surah Ar-Rahman.

q.en: Under which caliph was the Quran first gathered into one compiled copy?

e.en: After the Battle of Yamamah, Abu Bakr had Zayd ibn Thabit gather the Quran into one compilation.

q.en: Which caliph sent standard copies of the Mushaf to the major cities?

e.en: Uthman had copies made from Abu Bakr's compilation and sent them to the provinces.

q.en: Which surah is the last in the order of the Mushaf?

e.en: An-Nas (114) closes the Mushaf.

q.en: Which two surahs are known as al-Mu'awwidhatayn?

e.en: They are the two surahs of seeking refuge; the Prophet ﷺ recited them for protection.

q.en: Which story does the Quran call 'the best of stories'?

e.en: Allah says: 'We relate to you the best of stories' at the opening of Surah Yusuf.

q.en: Which surah tells the story of the young men of the cave?

e.en: Al-Kahf (18) is named after the cave in which the believing youths slept.

q.en: Which surah is named after iron?

e.en: Al-Hadid (57) mentions that Allah sent down iron with great strength and benefit.

q.en: Which Companion is the only one mentioned by name in the Quran?

e.en: Zayd is named in Surah Al-Ahzab.

q.en: Over roughly how many years was the Quran revealed?

e.en: Revelation began when the Prophet ﷺ was 40 and continued until his passing at 63.

q.en: The Quran calls itself 'Al-Furqan'. What does it mean?

e.en: Al-Furqan distinguishes truth from falsehood; Surah 25 carries this name.

q.en: Which surah is recited in every rak'ah of salah?

e.en: The Prophet ﷺ said there is no prayer for one who does not recite the Opening of the Book.

q.en: Which surah of thirty verses intercedes for its reciter?

e.en: The Prophet ﷺ said a surah of thirty verses (Al-Mulk) intercedes for its companion until he is forgiven.

q.en: Which surah tells of the army of the elephant?

e.en: Al-Fil (105) recalls how Allah destroyed Abrahah's army that came to attack the Kaaba.

q.en: Which prophet was swallowed by a great fish?

e.en: Yunus called upon Allah from the darkness inside the fish and was saved.

q.en: Surah Al-Masad (Tabbat) was revealed about whom?

e.en: It was revealed about Abu Lahab, the Prophet's uncle who opposed him, and his wife.

q.en: How many verses does Surah Al-Baqarah have?

e.en: Al-Baqarah ends at verse 286 with the dua 'Rabbana la tu'akhidhna…'.

q.en: In which city was the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ born?

e.en: He ﷺ was born in Makkah, in the clan of Banu Hashim of Quraysh.

q.en: In which year was the Prophet ﷺ born?

en: The Year of the Elephant (c. 570 CE)

e.en: He ﷺ was born in the year Abrahah attacked Makkah with elephants.

q.en: What was the name of the Prophet's father?

e.en: His father Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib passed away before he ﷺ was born.

q.en: What was the name of the Prophet's mother?

e.en: Aminah passed away at al-Abwa when he ﷺ was about six years old.

q.en: Which grandfather took care of the Prophet ﷺ after his mother passed away?

e.en: His grandfather Abd al-Muttalib cared for him until he passed away two years later.

q.en: Which uncle raised the Prophet ﷺ and protected him?

e.en: Abu Talib raised him from age eight and protected him in Makkah.

q.en: What was the name of the Prophet's wet-nurse in the desert?

e.en: He ﷺ spent his early childhood with Halimah of Banu Sa'd.

q.en: Who was the Prophet's first wife?

e.en: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, mother of the believers, was his first wife and first to believe.

q.en: In which cave did the first revelation come?

e.en: He ﷺ used to worship in the cave of Hira on Jabal an-Nur.

q.en: How old was the Prophet ﷺ when the revelation began?

e.en: Revelation began at the age of forty.

q.en: To which city did the Prophet ﷺ migrate?

e.en: In the Hijrah he ﷺ migrated to Yathrib, which became Madinat an-Nabi.

q.en: Who accompanied the Prophet ﷺ on the Hijrah?

e.en: Abu Bakr is 'the second of two' mentioned in the Quran.

q.en: In which cave did the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr hide during the Hijrah?

e.en: They stayed three nights in the cave of Thawr south of Makkah.

q.en: Which was the first masjid built by the Prophet ﷺ?

e.en: He ﷺ built Quba on arrival near Madinah; it is 'founded on taqwa'.

q.en: Which was the first major battle in Islam?

e.en: The Battle of Badr took place in Ramadan, 2 AH.

q.en: About how many Muslims fought at Badr?

e.en: Around 313 Companions faced an army of about a thousand.

q.en: Whose idea was digging the trench (Khandaq) around Madinah?

e.en: Salman suggested the Persian practice of defending with a trench in 5 AH.

q.en: In which year was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah?

e.en: The treaty was agreed in Dhul Qa'dah 6 AH; the Quran calls it a clear victory.

q.en: In which year was Makkah conquered?

e.en: The Conquest of Makkah took place in Ramadan, 8 AH.

q.en: In which year was the Farewell Hajj?

e.en: The Prophet ﷺ performed his only Hajj in 10 AH.

q.en: At what age did the Prophet ﷺ pass away?

e.en: He ﷺ passed away at sixty-three in Madinah.

q.en: Where is the Prophet ﷺ buried?

en: In Aishah's room, now within Masjid an-Nabawi

e.en: He ﷺ was buried where he passed away, in the room of Aishah.

q.en: Why is one year called 'the Year of Sorrow'?

en: Khadijah and Abu Talib passed away

e.en: Both his wife Khadijah and his uncle Abu Talib passed away in the same year.

q.en: What gift was given on the night of Isra and Mi'raj?

e.en: The five prayers were made obligatory on the night of the Ascension.

q.en: On the Isra, the Prophet ﷺ was taken from Masjid al-Haram to…

e.en: 'Glory be to Him who took His servant by night… to al-Masjid al-Aqsa.'

q.en: What title did the people of Makkah give the Prophet ﷺ before prophethood?

e.en: Quraysh called him al-Sadiq al-Amin for his honesty.

q.en: Who was the first person to believe in the Prophet ﷺ?

e.en: Khadijah believed in him from the first revelation; Abu Bakr was the first free man, Ali the first child.

q.en: Who was the first muezzin of Islam?

e.en: The Prophet ﷺ chose Bilal for his beautiful, strong voice.

q.en: Where did the first group of Muslims migrate to escape persecution?

e.en: They migrated to the just Christian king, an-Najashi.

q.en: In which battle did the archers leave their positions?

e.en: At Uhud in 3 AH some archers left the hill, and the Muslims suffered losses.

q.en: Which uncle of the Prophet ﷺ was martyred at Uhud?

e.en: Hamzah, 'Sayyid ash-Shuhada', was martyred at Uhud.

q.en: Which daughter of the Prophet ﷺ married Ali?

e.en: Fatimah az-Zahra married Ali ibn Abi Talib; she is the leader of the women of Paradise.

q.en: Which town did the Prophet ﷺ visit for support, where he was stoned?

e.en: In Ta'if he ﷺ was rejected and stoned, yet he prayed for their descendants.

q.en: With whom were the Pledges of Aqabah made?

e.en: The Ansar of Yathrib pledged at Aqabah, opening the way for the Hijrah.

q.en: What was the name of the Prophet's camel on the Hijrah?

e.en: Al-Qaswa knelt at the site that became Masjid an-Nabawi.

q.en: Who narrated the hadith 'Actions are only by intentions'?

e.en: It opens Sahih al-Bukhari and is narrated by Umar from the Prophet ﷺ.

q.en: Which book is considered the most authentic after the Quran?

e.en: The scholars of hadith hold Sahih al-Bukhari, then Sahih Muslim, as the most authentic books after the Quran.

q.en: Who compiled Sahih Muslim?

e.en: Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj of Nishapur (d. 261 AH) compiled it.

q.en: What are the six major hadith collections called?

e.en: Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, an-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah are known as the Six Books.

q.en: Which Companion narrated the most hadith?

e.en: Abu Hurayrah narrated over 5,000 hadith; he stayed close to the Prophet ﷺ to learn.

q.en: The famous 'Hadith of Jibril' explains which three levels of the religion?

e.en: Jibril came as a man and asked about Islam, Iman, Ihsan and the Hour.

q.en: How did the Prophet ﷺ define Ihsan?

en: To worship Allah as though you see Him

e.en: '…and if you do not see Him, He surely sees you.'

q.en: Islam is built upon how many pillars?

e.en: Shahadah, salah, zakat, Hajj and fasting Ramadan.

q.en: Complete: 'None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother…'

e.en: Wanting good for others is part of complete faith.

q.en: According to the hadith, who is truly strong?

en: One who controls himself when angry

e.en: 'The strong man is not the good wrestler; the strong man is the one who controls himself when angry.'

q.en: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about smiling at your brother?

e.en: 'Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity.'

q.en: Which deed did the Prophet ﷺ call 'half of faith'?

e.en: 'Purity is half of faith.'

q.en: Who are 'the best of you' according to the hadith?

en: Those who learn the Quran and teach it

e.en: 'The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.'

q.en: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should…

e.en: Guarding the tongue is a sign of faith.

q.en: What is a Hadith Qudsi?

en: Words from Allah conveyed by the Prophet ﷺ in his own wording

e.en: Its meaning is from Allah, its wording from the Prophet ﷺ, and it is not recited as Quran.

q.en: What does 'mutawatir' mean in hadith science?

en: Narrated by so many that agreeing on a lie is impossible

e.en: Mutawatir reports give certain knowledge.

q.en: What is the chain of narrators of a hadith called?

e.en: The isnad is the chain; Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said it is part of the religion.

q.en: What is the text of a hadith called?

e.en: The matn is the actual wording after the chain.

q.en: Who compiled the famous 'Forty Hadith' (al-Arba'in)?

e.en: Imam Yahya ibn Sharaf an-Nawawi (d. 676 AH) gathered 42 foundational hadith.

q.en: Who compiled al-Muwatta?

e.en: Imam Malik ibn Anas of Madinah compiled it, one of the earliest hadith books.

q.en: Who compiled the Musnad, a huge collection arranged by Companion?

e.en: The Musnad of Imam Ahmad contains around 27,000 narrations.

q.en: Complete: 'The religion is…'

e.en: 'The religion is sincerity: to Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims and their common folk.'

q.en: What should you do with something you are in doubt about?

en: Leave it for what you are not in doubt about

e.en: 'Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.'

q.en: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about making things easy?

en: Make things easy and do not make them difficult

e.en: 'Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not drive people away.'

q.en: Which deeds are most beloved to Allah?

en: The most consistent, even if small

e.en: Consistency is beloved to Allah.

q.en: Modesty (haya) is described in the hadith as…

e.en: 'Haya is a branch of iman.'

q.en: Who is a true Muslim according to the hadith?

en: One from whose tongue and hand people are safe

e.en: 'The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.'

q.en: Which two phrases are 'light on the tongue, heavy on the scale'?

en: Subhan Allahi wa bihamdihi, Subhan Allahil-Azim

e.en: These two phrases are beloved to the Most Merciful.

q.en: Who did the Prophet ﷺ say most deserves your good companionship?

en: Your mother (said three times), then your father

e.en: He ﷺ said 'your mother' three times, then 'your father'.

q.en: Imam al-Bukhari was from which city?

e.en: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari was born in Bukhara (in today's Uzbekistan) in 194 AH.

q.en: Whoever relieves a believer of a hardship in this world…

en: Allah will relieve him of a hardship on the Day of Judgement

e.en: Helping others brings Allah's help.

q.en: According to the hadith, what does Allah look at?

e.en: 'Allah does not look at your forms or your wealth, but at your hearts and deeds.'

q.en: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about whoever treads a path seeking knowledge?

en: Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise

e.en: Seeking knowledge is a road to Paradise.

q.en: How many obligatory (fard) daily prayers are there?

e.en: Five daily prayers were made obligatory on the night of the Mi'raj.

q.en: How many fard rak'ahs are in Fajr?

e.en: Fajr has two fard rak'ahs.

q.en: How many fard rak'ahs are in Maghrib?

e.en: Maghrib is three rak'ahs for both resident and traveller.

q.en: What percentage of zakatable wealth is given as zakat?

e.en: Zakat on money and trade goods is one fortieth (2.5%).

q.en: How long must wealth above the nisab be held before zakat is due?

e.en: Zakat is due after a full lunar year passes on the nisab.

q.en: When should Zakat al-Fitr be given?

e.en: The Prophet ﷺ ordered it to be given before people go out to the Eid prayer.

q.en: When may tayammum (dry ablution) be performed?

en: Whenever one is in a hurry
When water is unavailable or cannot be used

e.en: '…and you find no water, then seek clean earth.'

q.en: Which day of Hajj is the Day of Arafah?

e.en: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Hajj is Arafah.'

q.en: What is the ruling of the Jumu'ah prayer for adult resident men?

e.en: 'O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer on Friday, hasten to the remembrance of Allah.'

q.en: At which of these times is prayer prohibited?

e.en: Prayer is not offered as the sun rises, at its zenith, and as it sets.

q.en: How many rak'ahs of Taraweeh do the four madhhabs hold as the established practice?

e.en: Twenty rak'ahs is the practice from the time of Umar in all four schools (the Malikis also record 36 in old Madinah).

q.en: What is the direction faced in salah called?

e.en: Muslims face the Kaaba in Makkah.

q.en: What makes ghusl (full bath) obligatory?

e.en: 'If you are in a state of janabah, purify yourselves.'

q.en: What is the call made just before the fard prayer begins in the masjid?

e.en: The adhan calls people; the iqamah announces the prayer is starting.

q.en: When a traveller shortens Dhuhr, it becomes how many rak'ahs?

e.en: Four-rak'ah prayers are shortened to two when travelling.

q.en: For a traveller, how long may one wipe over leather socks (khuffs)?

e.en: The Prophet ﷺ set three days and nights for the traveller and one day and night for the resident.

q.en: Which act ends the salah?

e.en: 'Its closing is the taslim.'

q.en: How many fard (obligatory) acts of wudu are there?

e.en: Hanafi: four — washing the face, the arms to the elbows, wiping a quarter of the head, and washing the feet.

questions.s: Quran 5:6; Nur al-Idah; Safinat an-Naja; ar-Risalah; Dalil at-Talib

e.en: Shafi'i: six — intention, face, arms, wiping part of the head, feet, and order (tartib).
Maliki: seven — intention, face, arms, wiping the head, feet, rubbing (dalk) and continuity (muwalat).
Hanbali: six — face (with mouth and nose), arms, wiping the whole head with the ears, feet, order and continuity.

q.en: What is the ruling of the Witr prayer?

e.en: Hanafi: Witr is wajib — three rak'ahs with one salam and qunut before ruku.

questions.s: Sunan Abi Dawud 1419; al-Hidayah; al-Majmu'; al-Mughni

e.en: Shafi'i: Witr is a stressed sunnah, from one to eleven rak'ahs.
Maliki: Witr is a stressed sunnah, one rak'ah after a shaf' of two.
Hanbali: Witr is a stressed sunnah, at least one rak'ah.

q.en: Does touching a non-mahram adult of the opposite sex break wudu?

e.en: Hanafi: it does not break wudu; the Prophet ﷺ kissed one of his wives and prayed without renewing wudu.

questions.s: Quran 4:43; Sunan Abi Dawud 179; al-Majmu'; al-Mughni

e.en: Shafi'i: direct skin contact breaks wudu, from 'or you have touched women' (4:43).
Maliki: it breaks wudu only when there is desire, or the intention of pleasure.
Hanbali: it breaks wudu only when done with desire.

q.en: What should a follower do about reciting Al-Fatihah behind the imam?

en: Remain silent; the imam's recitation suffices
Recite it in the silent prayers, not the loud ones

e.en: Hanafi: the follower stays silent — 'whoever has an imam, the imam's recitation is his recitation'.

questions.s: Quran 7:204; Sunan Ibn Majah 850; Sahih al-Bukhari 756

e.en: Shafi'i: Al-Fatihah is obligatory on the follower in every rak'ah.
Maliki: recommended in silent prayers; in loud prayers the follower listens.
Hanbali: recommended in silent prayers and pauses; in loud prayers the follower listens.

q.en: Does bleeding from a wound break wudu?

en: Yes, if it flows beyond the spot
Only if the amount is large

e.en: Hanafi: blood that flows beyond the place of the wound breaks wudu.
Shafi'i: bleeding does not break wudu; only what exits the two passages does.
Maliki: bleeding does not break wudu.
Hanbali: a large amount of blood breaks wudu; a little does not.

q.en: When are the hands raised in salah (raf' al-yadayn)?

en: At the opening, before and after ruku

e.en: Hanafi: only at the opening takbir, following the narration of Ibn Mas'ud.
Shafi'i: at the opening, before ruku, after rising from ruku, and on standing for the third rak'ah.
Maliki: the relied-upon view is only at the opening takbir.
Hanbali: at the opening, before ruku and after rising from it.

q.en: When does the time of Asr begin?

en: When an object's shadow equals its length
When an object's shadow is twice its length

e.en: Hanafi (Imam Abu Hanifa): when the shadow reaches twice the object's length (beyond the noon shadow). Noor Pro's Hanafi Asr setting uses this.
Shafi'i: when the shadow equals the object's length (beyond the noon shadow).
Maliki: when the shadow equals the object's length.
Hanbali: when the shadow equals the object's length.

q.en: Someone deliberately eats during a Ramadan fast without excuse. What is due?

en: Make up the day and the kaffarah (expiation)

e.en: Hanafi: qada plus kaffarah (sixty consecutive days of fasting), as deliberate eating violates the fast's sanctity.
Shafi'i: qada and sincere repentance; kaffarah is only for intercourse.
Maliki: qada plus kaffarah for deliberately breaking a Ramadan fast.
Hanbali: qada and repentance; kaffarah is only for intercourse.

q.en: You eat by forgetting while fasting in Ramadan. What happens?

en: The fast remains valid; carry on
Carry on, then make up the day later

e.en: Hanafi: the fast is valid — 'Allah fed him and gave him drink'.
Shafi'i: the fast is valid and nothing is owed.
Maliki: continue fasting the day, and make up an obligatory fast later.
Hanbali: the fast is valid and nothing is owed.

q.en: Where is the prostration of forgetfulness (sujud as-sahw) done?

en: Before for an omission, after for an addition

e.en: Hanafi: after one salam to the right, then two sajdahs, tashahhud and salam.
Shafi'i: before the salam in all cases.
Maliki: before the salam for an omission, after it for an addition.
Hanbali: generally before the salam, except in the cases the Sunnah specifies after it.

q.en: How many extra takbirs are said in the Eid prayer?

en: 7 in the first, 5 in the second
6 in the first, 5 in the second

e.en: Hanafi: three extra takbirs in each rak'ah, from Ibn Mas'ud.
Shafi'i: seven in the first rak'ah after the opening takbir, five in the second.
Maliki: six in the first after the opening takbir, five in the second.
Hanbali: six in the first after the opening takbir, five in the second.

q.en: What is the ruling of the Eid prayer?

e.en: Hanafi: wajib on those for whom Jumu'ah is obligatory.
Shafi'i: a stressed sunnah.
Maliki: a stressed sunnah.
Hanbali: a communal obligation (fard kifayah).

q.en: Shortening the four-rak'ah prayers (qasr) while travelling is…

en: Wajib — praying four is a mistake
A permitted concession; shortening is better

e.en: Hanafi: shortening is required for the traveller; Aishah said the prayer was first made two rak'ahs.
Shafi'i: a concession; shortening is better on a long journey.
Maliki: shortening is a stressed sunnah.
Hanbali: a concession, and shortening is better.

q.en: May a traveller combine Dhuhr with Asr?

en: Yes, it is allowed when travelling
No — only at Arafah and Muzdalifah in Hajj

e.en: Hanafi: each prayer is prayed in its own time; true combining is only at Arafah and Muzdalifah. A traveller may pray Dhuhr late in its time and Asr early in its time.
Shafi'i: a traveller on a long journey may combine Dhuhr with Asr and Maghrib with Isha.
Maliki: combining is allowed for a traveller, with conditions.
Hanbali: combining is allowed for a traveller.

q.en: What is the ruling of Qurbani (udhiyah) for one who has the nisab?

e.en: Hanafi: wajib on a resident adult Muslim who owns the nisab on the days of sacrifice.
Shafi'i: a stressed sunnah.
Maliki: a stressed sunnah.
Hanbali: a stressed sunnah.

q.en: After Al-Fatihah in a loud prayer, how is 'Ameen' said?

e.en: Hanafi: Ameen is said quietly.
Shafi'i: Ameen is said aloud in the loud prayers.
Maliki: Ameen is said quietly.
Hanbali: Ameen is said aloud in the loud prayers.

q.en: Where are the hands placed while standing in salah (for men)?

en: Folded above the navel, below the chest

e.en: Hanafi: right over left, below the navel.
Shafi'i: right over left, above the navel and below the chest.
Maliki: the well-known view is releasing the arms in the obligatory prayer; folding is allowed in voluntary prayers.
Hanbali: right over left, below the navel.

q.en: Is qunut recited regularly in the Fajr prayer?

en: No — qunut is in Witr, and in Fajr only at times of calamity

e.en: Hanafi: qunut is in Witr; in Fajr only at times of calamity (qunut an-nazilah).
Shafi'i: qunut is a sunnah in the second rak'ah of Fajr after ruku.
Maliki: qunut in Fajr is recommended, quietly before ruku.
Hanbali: qunut is in Witr; in Fajr only at times of calamity.

q.en: For one who is not travelling, how long may khuffs be wiped?

e.en: Hanafi: one day and night for the resident.
Shafi'i: one day and night for the resident.
Maliki: no fixed limit, though removing them weekly (on Friday) is recommended.
Hanbali: one day and night for the resident.

q.en: How many articles of faith (arkan al-iman) are there?

e.en: Belief in Allah, His angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, and the decree — its good and bad.

q.en: Which of these is a pillar of Islam rather than an article of faith?

e.en: Hajj is one of the five pillars of Islam; the six articles of faith are matters of belief.

q.en: What does Tawhid mean?

e.en: Tawhid is believing that Allah is One, without partner, in His essence, attributes and actions.

q.en: What are the two great schools of Sunni creed (aqidah)?

e.en: The Ash'ari and Maturidi schools are the creed of Ahl as-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah; the madhhabs are schools of fiqh.

q.en: Imam Abu Mansur al-Maturidi was from which city?

e.en: Imam al-Maturidi (d. 333 AH) of Samarqand systematised the creed of the Hanafi scholars.

q.en: Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari was a descendant of which Companion?

e.en: He descended from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari; the Prophet ﷺ praised the people of Abu Musa (Quran 5:54 commentary).

q.en: Complete the verse: 'There is nothing…'

e.en: 'There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.'

q.en: Allah exists without a beginning. What is this attribute called?

e.en: Qidam: Allah has no beginning. Baqa': He has no end.

q.en: Allah exists without an end. What is this attribute called?

e.en: 'Everything will perish except His Face.'

q.en: 'Mukhalafatuhu lil-hawadith' means that Allah…

en: is unlike His creation in every way

e.en: Nothing in creation resembles Allah, and He resembles nothing in creation.

q.en: Who will be given the 'Praised Station' (al-Maqam al-Mahmud) of the great intercession?

e.en: On the Day of Judgement people go to the prophets until they come to Muhammad ﷺ, who intercedes.

q.en: Who is the final prophet?

e.en: He ﷺ is 'the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets'.

q.en: Prophets are protected from sin. What is this protection called?

e.en: All prophets are protected (ma'sum) from sins, as they are the examples to be followed.

q.en: A wondrous event granted to a saint (wali) is called…

e.en: Ahl as-Sunnah affirm the karamat of the awliya, as narrated about Maryam and the Companions of the Cave.

q.en: What is the greatest miracle of the Prophet ﷺ?

e.en: Every prophet was given signs; 'what I have been given is the revelation'.

q.en: What do Ahl as-Sunnah believe about seeing Allah in Paradise?

en: The believers will see Him, without 'how' or likeness

e.en: 'Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord.' Ahl as-Sunnah affirm the vision without encompassing or likeness.

q.en: Which classic creed was written by Imam Abu Ja'far at-Tahawi?

e.en: It records the creed of Abu Hanifa and his two companions, accepted by all Ahl as-Sunnah.

q.en: 'Al-Fiqh al-Akbar', an early creed, is attributed to which imam?

e.en: It is attributed to Imam Abu Hanifa; 'the greater fiqh' means creed.

q.en: Which two angels question a person in the grave?

e.en: The Prophet ﷺ named the two questioning angels Munkar and Nakir.

q.en: What is the bridge over Hell that all must cross called?

e.en: The Sirat is set over Hell; believers cross according to their deeds.

q.en: Which book was revealed to Prophet Musa?

e.en: The Tawrah was given to Musa, the Zabur to Dawud, the Injil to Isa.

q.en: What is the angel of death called in the Quran?

e.en: 'The Angel of Death who has been put in charge of you will take your souls.' He is commonly called Azra'il.

q.en: Which angel will blow the Trumpet?

e.en: Israfil will blow the Sur on the Last Day.

q.en: What is shirk?

e.en: Allah does not forgive shirk for one who dies upon it, and forgives other than that for whom He wills.

q.en: Belief in Qadar (the Divine Decree) means believing…

en: the future is unknown to Allah
humans create their own fate alone
everything, good and bad, happens by Allah's decree

e.en: It is the sixth article of faith; people still choose and are accountable.

q.en: In the Maturidi school, faith (iman) in its essence is…

en: Conviction of the heart and affirmation by the tongue

e.en: Deeds complete faith and are its fruit, but are not part of its essence; the Ash'aris define it as the heart's conviction, with the tongue as a condition of worldly rulings.

q.en: How many prophets are mentioned by name in the Quran?

e.en: Twenty-five prophets are named; there were many more, whom Allah sent to every nation.

q.en: Who was the first prophet?

e.en: Adam (peace be upon him) was the first human and the first prophet.

q.en: Which of these is NOT one of the Ulul 'Azm (prophets of firm resolve)?

e.en: The Ulul 'Azm are Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and Muhammad (peace be upon them).

q.en: What do Muslims believe about Prophet Isa (Jesus)?

en: He was raised alive to Allah and will return before the Hour
He was the son of God

e.en: 'They did not kill him, nor crucify him… rather Allah raised him to Himself.' He will descend near the end of time.

q.en: Who is the Dajjal?

en: The great false messiah who appears before the Hour

e.en: The Prophet ﷺ taught us to seek refuge from the trial of the Dajjal in every prayer.

q.en: From which family did the Prophet ﷺ say the Mahdi will be?

en: His family (Ahl al-Bayt), from the descendants of Fatimah

e.en: 'The Mahdi is from my family, from the descendants of Fatimah.'

q.en: According to Ahl as-Sunnah, who is the best of the Companions?

en: Abu Bakr, then Umar, then Uthman, then Ali

e.en: Ahl as-Sunnah rank the four caliphs in the order of their caliphate and love all the Companions and the Ahl al-Bayt.

q.en: Seeking Allah's help through the rank of the Prophet ﷺ (tawassul) is…

en: Permissible according to the majority of Ahl as-Sunnah

e.en: The Prophet ﷺ taught a blind man to say 'I turn to You through Your Prophet Muhammad, the Prophet of mercy'.

q.en: Imam at-Tahawi wrote that Allah is not contained by…

e.en: 'He is not contained by the six directions as created things are.' Allah is free of place and direction.

q.en: Who was the first caliph after the Prophet ﷺ?

e.en: The Companions pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr in 11 AH.

q.en: Who was the second caliph?

e.en: Umar al-Faruq led from 13 to 23 AH.

q.en: Who was the third caliph?

e.en: Uthman Dhun-Nurayn led from 23 to 35 AH.

q.en: Who was the fourth caliph?

e.en: Ali led from 35 to 40 AH.

q.en: Under which caliph did the Hijri calendar begin to be used?

e.en: Umar, with the Companions, dated the calendar from the Hijrah.

q.en: Which year of the Gregorian calendar is 1 AH?

e.en: The Hijrah to Madinah took place in 622 CE.

q.en: Under which caliph did the Muslims enter Jerusalem peacefully?

e.en: Umar came in person to receive the city in about 637 CE.

q.en: Which sultan conquered Constantinople in 1453?

e.en: Mehmed II, 'al-Fatih', conquered Constantinople, fulfilling a hadith about its conquest.

q.en: Who liberated Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187?

e.en: After the Battle of Hattin, Salahuddin entered Jerusalem and spared its people.

q.en: Who led the Muslim army into al-Andalus (Spain) in 711?

e.en: Gibraltar (Jabal Tariq) is named after him.

q.en: Which dynasty ruled after the Rightly Guided Caliphs?

e.en: The Umayyad caliphate ruled from Damascus from 41 AH (661 CE).

q.en: What was the capital of the Abbasid caliphate?

e.en: Al-Mansur founded Baghdad in 762 CE.

q.en: The 'House of Wisdom' (Bayt al-Hikmah) was in which city?

e.en: It was a great library and centre of translation under the Abbasids.

q.en: Which Umayyad ruler is often called the 'fifth Rightly Guided Caliph'?

e.en: His justice and piety led the scholars to count him with the Rightly Guided Caliphs.

q.en: Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal?

e.en: Shah Jahan built it in Agra in memory of Mumtaz Mahal.

q.en: Who brought Islam to Sindh in 711–712?

e.en: The young Umayyad commander Muhammad ibn Qasim conquered Sindh and Multan.

q.en: Who founded the Ottoman state?

e.en: The Ottomans are named after Osman Ghazi.

q.en: In which year did the Mongols sack Baghdad?

e.en: Hulagu's army destroyed Baghdad and ended the Abbasid caliphate there.

q.en: Al-Azhar is in which city?

e.en: Founded in 970 CE, it became a great Sunni centre of learning.

q.en: Who founded the University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez?

e.en: Fatimah al-Fihri founded it in 859 CE; it is among the oldest universities still operating.

q.en: The great traveller Ibn Battuta was from which city?

e.en: He set out from Tangier in 1325 and travelled for nearly thirty years.

q.en: Which scholar's name gave us the word 'algorithm'?

e.en: Al-Khwarizmi wrote the book from which 'algebra' also gets its name.

q.en: Who wrote 'The Canon of Medicine'?

e.en: Ibn Sina's al-Qanun was a standard medical text for centuries.

q.en: Mansa Musa, famous for his Hajj with great wealth, ruled which empire?

e.en: Mansa Musa made his Hajj in 1324.

q.en: In which year was the Ottoman caliphate abolished?

e.en: The Turkish Grand National Assembly abolished it on 3 March 1924.

q.en: Who built the Dome of the Rock?

e.en: The Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik completed it around 691 CE.

q.en: Which ruler was known as the 'Tiger of Mysore'?

e.en: Tipu Sultan resisted the British until he was martyred in 1799.

q.en: Who was the field commander of the Muslims at the Battle of Yarmouk (636)?

e.en: Khalid, 'the Sword of Allah', led the field command at Yarmouk.

q.en: Who commanded the Muslims at the Battle of al-Qadisiyyah?

e.en: Sa'd led the army that defeated the Sasanian Persians.

q.en: Which Seljuk sultan won the Battle of Manzikert in 1071?

e.en: The victory opened Anatolia to the Muslims.

q.en: Who founded the Mughal Empire?

e.en: Babur won at Panipat in 1526.

q.en: Which caliph was known as 'Dhun-Nurayn' (possessor of two lights)?

e.en: He married two daughters of the Prophet ﷺ, Ruqayyah and then Umm Kulthum.

q.en: Which Abbasid caliph was famous in the time of Imam Abu Yusuf and the 'Thousand and One Nights' tales?

e.en: Harun ar-Rashid ruled 786–809 CE; Imam Abu Yusuf was his chief judge.

q.en: Tasawwuf is the science of which level of the religion described in the Hadith of Jibril?

e.en: Ihsan — worshipping Allah as though you see Him — is the heart of tasawwuf.

q.en: Shaykh Abdul Qadir al-Jilani is buried in which city?

e.en: Ghawth al-A'zam Shaykh Abdul Qadir al-Jilani (d. 561 AH) taught and is buried in Baghdad.

q.en: Which Sufi order is named after Shaykh Abdul Qadir al-Jilani?

e.en: The Qadiri path traces to him and spread across the Muslim world.

q.en: Khwaja Mu'in ad-Din Chishti, 'Gharib Nawaz', is buried in…

e.en: He came to India in the 12th century; his dargah is in Ajmer Sharif.

q.en: Data Ganj Bakhsh Ali al-Hujwiri wrote which classic of tasawwuf?

e.en: Kashf al-Mahjub is among the earliest Persian works on tasawwuf; he is buried in Lahore.

q.en: Which Sufi order is named after Shaykh Baha' ad-Din of Bukhara?

e.en: Shaykh Baha' ad-Din Naqshband (d. 791 AH) gave the order its name.

q.en: Which scholar is called 'Hujjat al-Islam' and wrote 'Ihya Ulum ad-Din'?

e.en: Imam Abu Hamid al-Ghazali (d. 505 AH) united fiqh, creed and tasawwuf in the Ihya.

q.en: Which early Sufi is called 'Sayyid at-Ta'ifah' (master of the group)?

e.en: Al-Junayd said: 'Our path is bound by the Quran and the Sunnah.'

q.en: Rabi'ah al-Adawiyyah, known for her pure love of Allah, lived in which city?

e.en: She was a renowned worshipper of Basra in the 2nd century AH.

q.en: Hasan al-Basri belonged to which generation?

e.en: Hasan al-Basri (d. 110 AH) met many Companions and is a pillar of early zuhd.

q.en: 'Awarif al-Ma'arif' was written by the founder of which order?

e.en: Shaykh Shihab ad-Din Umar as-Suhrawardi (d. 632 AH) wrote it.

q.en: Hazrat Nizam ad-Din Awliya, 'Mahbub-e-Ilahi', is buried in…

e.en: His dargah is in Nizamuddin, Delhi; Amir Khusrau was his disciple.

q.en: Baba Farid ad-Din Ganj-e-Shakar is buried in…

e.en: A great Chishti shaykh, the teacher of Nizam ad-Din Awliya.

q.en: Khwaja Qutb ad-Din Bakhtiyar Kaki, successor of Khwaja Gharib Nawaz, is buried in…

e.en: The Qutub Minar area is named in his honour.

q.en: Who is known as 'Mujaddid Alf Thani' (Renewer of the second millennium)?

e.en: Imam Rabbani Ahmad Sirhindi (d. 1034 AH) of the Naqshbandi order, author of the Maktubat.

q.en: Shah Waliullah Muhaddith Dehlawi wrote which famous book?

e.en: He was a great muhaddith and Sufi of Delhi (d. 1176 AH).

q.en: Mawlana Jalal ad-Din Rumi wrote which famous poem?

e.en: Rumi is buried in Konya; his Masnavi is a vast poem of spiritual teaching.

q.en: Who wrote 'ar-Risalah', a foundational manual of tasawwuf?

e.en: Al-Qushayri (d. 465 AH) wrote it to show tasawwuf's roots in the Quran, Sunnah and sound creed.

q.en: Which Sufi order is named after Shaykh Abu al-Hasan ash-Shadhili?

e.en: Shaykh ash-Shadhili (d. 656 AH) taught in North Africa and Egypt.

q.en: Who wrote 'al-Hikam', the famous aphorisms of tasawwuf?

e.en: A Shadhili master of Alexandria (d. 709 AH).

q.en: Which order traces to Sayyid Ahmad ar-Rifa'i of Iraq?

e.en: Sayyid Ahmad al-Kabir ar-Rifa'i (d. 578 AH) was known for his humility.

q.en: The Prophet ﷺ told Umar about a man from Yemen whose dua is accepted. Who was he?

e.en: He was devoted to his mother; the Prophet ﷺ told Umar to ask him for forgiveness.

q.en: Khwaja Bandanawaz Gesudaraz is buried in which city?

e.en: A Chishti master (d. 825 AH) who brought the Chishti path to the Deccan.

q.en: 'Futuh al-Ghayb' is a collection of discourses by…

e.en: It contains his talks on tawhid, trust and surrender to Allah.

q.en: What does 'dhikr' mean?

e.en: 'Truly, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.'

q.en: What does 'tazkiyat an-nafs' mean?

e.en: 'He has succeeded who purifies it.'

q.en: A 'silsilah' in tasawwuf is…

en: the chain of spiritual teachers back to the Prophet ﷺ

e.en: Each order's silsilah connects its shaykhs, link by link, to the Prophet ﷺ.

q.en: The pledge (bay'ah) given to a shaykh follows which practice in the Quran?

en: The pledge the Companions gave the Prophet ﷺ

e.en: 'Indeed those who pledge allegiance to you, pledge allegiance to Allah.'

q.en: The 'nafs al-mutma'innah' is…

e.en: 'O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing.'

q.en: The 'nafs al-ammarah' is…

e.en: Yusuf said: 'The soul is surely a commander of evil, except where my Lord has mercy.'

q.en: In a Hadith Qudsi, Allah declares war on whoever shows enmity to…

e.en: 'Whoever shows enmity to a wali of Mine, I declare war on him.'

q.en: What does the Quran say about the awliya of Allah?

en: No fear shall be on them, nor shall they grieve

e.en: 'Surely the friends of Allah — no fear shall be on them nor shall they grieve: those who believe and are mindful of Him.'

q.en: In the subcontinent, what does 'urs' commemorate?

en: The anniversary of a wali's passing (wisal)

e.en: It marks the day the wali met his Lord, with Quran, dhikr and remembrance.

q.en: Makhdum Ali Mahimi, the scholar-saint of Mahim, was from which coast?

e.en: Makhdum Ali al-Mahimi (d. 835 AH) wrote the tafsir Tabsir ar-Rahman.

q.en: What do we say before eating?

e.en: The Prophet ﷺ told a boy: 'Say Bismillah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is near you.'

q.en: If you forget Bismillah at the start of a meal, what do you say?

e.en: 'In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end.'

q.en: What do we say when we sneeze?

e.en: The one who hears replies 'Yarhamuk Allah', and the sneezer answers 'Yahdikumullah wa yuslihu balakum'.

q.en: Which dua is said before entering the toilet?

en: Allahumma inni a'udhu bika minal-khubuthi wal-khaba'ith

e.en: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the male and female devils.'

q.en: What is said on leaving the toilet?

e.en: The Prophet ﷺ would say 'Ghufranak' on coming out.

q.en: Which dua is said before sleeping?

e.en: 'In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.'

q.en: On waking up, the Prophet ﷺ would praise Allah who…

en: fed us and gave us drink
gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the return

e.en: 'Alhamdulillahil-ladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa ilayhin-nushur.'

q.en: Which dua is said on entering the masjid?

e.en: 'O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.'

q.en: Which dua is said on leaving the masjid?

e.en: 'O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty.'

q.en: Which dua did the Prophet ﷺ make most often?

en: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah

e.en: 'Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'

q.en: Whose dua was 'La ilaha illa anta, subhanaka, inni kuntu minaz-zalimin'?

e.en: He called with it from inside the fish; any Muslim who calls with it is answered.

q.en: Which is the Quranic dua for parents?

e.en: 'My Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small.'

q.en: Which is the Quranic dua for increase in knowledge?

e.en: 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge.'

q.en: What is the 'Sayyid al-Istighfar' (master of seeking forgiveness)?

en: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
Allahumma anta Rabbi, la ilaha illa ant, khalaqtani…

e.en: Whoever says it with conviction in the day and dies before evening is of the people of Paradise.

q.en: Which dua did the Prophet ﷺ teach Aishah for Laylat al-Qadr?

e.en: 'O Allah, You are Pardoning and love to pardon, so pardon me.'

q.en: Ibrahim said 'Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal-wakil' when…

en: he was thrown into the fire

e.en: 'Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.'

q.en: Which dua is recited when setting off on a journey?

e.en: 'Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have done it ourselves.'

q.en: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when visiting the sick?

en: La ba'sa, tahurun in sha Allah

e.en: 'No harm, it is a purification, if Allah wills.'

q.en: What is said when leaving home?

en: Bismillahi tawakkaltu 'alallah, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah

e.en: The one who says it is guided, sufficed and protected.

q.en: Which dua did the Prophet ﷺ say on breaking the fast?

en: Dhahabaz-zama'u wabtallatil-'uruq wa thabatal-ajru in sha Allah

e.en: 'The thirst is gone, the veins are moistened, and the reward is confirmed, if Allah wills.'

q.en: What is said on seeing the new crescent moon?

e.en: 'O Allah, bring it over us with blessing and faith, safety and Islam. My Lord and your Lord is Allah.'

q.en: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when it rained?

e.en: 'O Allah, (make it) a beneficial rain.'

q.en: What should we say when we feel angry?

e.en: The Prophet ﷺ said that saying it would take away the anger.

q.en: What do we say when a calamity strikes?

en: Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un

e.en: 'Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return' — then ask Allah for something better.

q.en: On which day did the Prophet ﷺ ask us to send abundant salawat on him?

e.en: 'Send abundant blessings on me on Friday, for they are presented to me.'

q.en: How many times is 'Bismillahil-ladhi la yadurru ma'asmihi shay'un…' recited morning and evening?

e.en: Whoever says it three times, nothing will harm him.

q.en: Which prophet prayed 'Rabbish-rah li sadri' (My Lord, expand my chest)?

e.en: Musa asked for ease before going to Fir'awn.

q.en: 'Rabbana zalamna anfusana…' was the dua of whom?

e.en: 'Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves; if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will be among the losers.'

q.en: Which Quranic dua asks for righteous spouses and children?

en: Rabbana hab lana min azwajina wa dhurriyyatina qurrata a'yun

e.en: '…the coolness of our eyes, and make us leaders of the God-fearing.'

q.en: Reciting which verse before sleeping keeps a guardian from Allah with you all night?

e.en: So the Prophet ﷺ confirmed in the story of Abu Hurayrah and the thief.

q.en: Which verses, recited at night, are 'sufficient' for a person?

en: The last two verses of Al-Baqarah

e.en: 'Whoever recites the last two verses of Surat al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him.'

q.en: What should we do when we hear the adhan?

e.en: Then send salawat and ask for al-Wasilah for the Prophet ﷺ.

q.en: What do we say when we see something we like?

e.en: Saying 'Ma sha Allah, la quwwata illa billah' and asking for barakah protects from the evil eye.

q.en: How many times do Muslims pray each day?

e.en: We pray Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.

q.en: What do we say before we eat?

e.en: We start with the name of Allah, and eat with our right hand.

q.en: What is the holy book of Muslims?

e.en: Allah sent the Quran to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

q.en: Who is the last Prophet?

e.en: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets.

q.en: In which month do Muslims fast?

e.en: We fast from Fajr to Maghrib every day of Ramadan.

q.en: In which city is the Kaaba?

e.en: Muslims all over the world face the Kaaba when they pray.

q.en: Which Prophet built the Ark?

e.en: Allah told Nuh to build a big ship before the flood.

q.en: Which Prophet was swallowed by a big fish?

e.en: Yunus prayed to Allah inside the fish and Allah saved him.

q.en: Which Prophet understood the speech of the ants?

e.en: Sulayman smiled when he heard an ant warn its friends.

q.en: What do we say when we sneeze?

e.en: Then the person who hears says 'Yarhamuk Allah'.

q.en: How do Muslims greet each other?

e.en: It means 'Peace be upon you.' Spreading salam brings love.

q.en: How do we reply to 'Assalamu alaykum'?

e.en: We reply with an equal or better greeting.

q.en: Which Prophet was thrown into a fire that became cool?

e.en: Allah said: 'O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim.'

q.en: Which Prophet's staff turned into a snake?

e.en: It was one of the signs Allah gave Musa before Fir'awn.

q.en: Who built the Kaaba with Prophet Ibrahim?

e.en: Father and son raised its walls and prayed to Allah.

q.en: What is washing before prayer called?

e.en: We wash our hands, mouth, nose, face, arms, wipe our head, and wash our feet.

q.en: What is the call to prayer called?

e.en: The muezzin calls the adhan five times a day.

q.en: Where do Muslims pray together?

e.en: The masjid is the house of Allah.

q.en: Which Eid comes after Ramadan?

e.en: On Eid al-Fitr we thank Allah after a month of fasting.

q.en: Which Eid is the festival of sacrifice?

e.en: It remembers Prophet Ibrahim's obedience to Allah.

q.en: Which angel brought Allah's message to the Prophets?

e.en: Jibril brought the Quran to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

q.en: How many pillars of Islam are there?

e.en: Shahadah, salah, zakat, fasting and Hajj.

q.en: What is the first pillar of Islam?

e.en: La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur Rasulullah.

q.en: What was the name of the Prophet's daughter who married Ali?

e.en: Fatimah az-Zahra was very beloved to the Prophet ﷺ.

q.en: Which Prophet dreamed of eleven stars, the sun and the moon?

e.en: Yusuf told his father about the dream when he was a boy.

q.en: In which city is Prophet Muhammad ﷺ buried?

e.en: His blessed resting place is in Masjid an-Nabawi.

q.en: On which day is the Jumu'ah prayer?

e.en: Friday is the best day of the week.

q.en: What does 'SubhanAllah' mean?

e.en: We say it when we see something amazing Allah has made.

q.en: What does 'Alhamdulillah' mean?

e.en: We thank Allah for everything He gives us.

q.en: What does 'In sha Allah' mean?

e.en: We say it when we talk about doing something in the future.

q.en: Which animal did the people of Prophet Salih harm?

e.en: The she-camel was a sign from Allah, and they were told not to harm it.

q.en: Which Prophet was given the Zabur?

e.en: Dawud praised Allah beautifully, and the mountains and birds praised with him.

q.en: Who was the mother of Prophet Isa?

e.en: Maryam was a very righteous woman chosen by Allah.

q.en: Who was the first muezzin?

e.en: Bilal had a beautiful voice and called the adhan for the Prophet ﷺ.

q.en: What should we say to someone who helps us?

e.en: It means 'May Allah reward you with good.'
